Date: 2027-04-20 | Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes

summary: Kickoff for AtlasWell Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, success criteria, security requirements (SSO, SOC2), preferred deployment (private VPC/dedicated), initial timeline and benchmarking plan. Agreed next steps and assigned action items.
topics: Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE for AtlasWell. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. CTO.
[00:12] Sam Ortega: Sam, VP Product.
[00:14] Lena Kim: Lena, head of eng.
[00:16] Ethan Liu: Ethan, CSM at Redwood.
[00:18] Ravi Desai: Ravi, SE - I'll own the infra bits.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Agenda is pretty straightforward — align on success criteria, security/compliance, decide target deployment (private vs dedicated vs hosted), and plan initial benchmarks.
[00:35] Priya: Sounds good. Our main goal is to replace a bunch of heuristic-driven routing with an LLM-powered triage layer. Need predictable latency under 250ms p95 for the user-facing flow and cost to be in control; otherwise exec won't sign off.
[00:50] Sam: And timeline — we want a pilot in prod-ish environment by mid-June, so about 7 weeks.
[00:56] Maya: Good, mid-June is reasonable. We'll map an onboarding plan. Ethan, do you want to run through success criteria template?
[01:05] Ethan: Sure. Priya already mentioned latency p95 target. Also accuracy/quality thresholds — sample prompts we evaluate weekly, and cost per 1k tokens target. We'll capture these in the onboarding doc.
[01:20] Priya: Also compliance — we handle PHI, so we need private deployment options and audit logs. SOC 2 is required. SSO via SAML, KMS key management, and retention controls.
[01:32] Maya: Understood. Redwood offers Private (VPC) and Dedicated. Private gives you a customer-managed VPC + KMS integration; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools but still hosted. For PHI we typically recommend Private or Private+airgap if needed.
[01:48] Priya: Right, can you send the SOC 2 and FedRAMP (if any) docs?
[01:52] Maya: We have SOC 2 report and compliance whitepaper. I'll send both. Links: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/soc2 and the onboarding checklist: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/checklist
[02:05] Lena: Quick technical Q — how's KV cache handled? We have a lot of repeated prefixes in requests.
[02:12] Ravi: Good call. Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce compute time; for long conversations we also support efficient KV eviction. In Dedicated/Private you can tune cache size and affinity.
[02:25] Lena: Any difference in behavior between hosted and private for cache?
[02:28] Ravi: Behavior is the same, but private gives you control over retention and network path. One caveat — cross-zone latencies can affect p95 if your VPC setup routes poorly. We'll make recommendations for subnet placement.
[02:44] Sam: On cost — we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI. OpenAI seemed easiest but cost was higher at scale; Anthropic had a good quality/cost balance. Curious how Redwood's pricing for dedicated compares.
[02:58] Maya: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity pricing — monthly commit with discounted per-token/instance rates. For the pilot we can offer a short-term trial rate; I'll attach pricing matrix after this call.
[03:12] Priya: How about quantization — can we run int8 to cut cost?
[03:16] Ravi: Yes, runtime supports int8 and mixed precision; we can recommend quantization profiles per model and workload. For your use-case, int8 with approximate-kv precision usually keeps quality within acceptable bounds. We'll run quality regression tests as part of the benchmark.
[03:33] Lena: Great. For the pilot data — what's the easiest way to share telemetry and sample traffic?
[03:38] Ethan: We usually accept a gzipped sample of 1 week of anonymized traffic — sample prompts, average seq lengths, token distribution, and failure cases. We'll use that to recommend model and batching config.
[03:49] Priya: We'll need to scrub PHI, but can provide synthetic or anonymized traffic. I'll loop in compliance.
[03:55] Sam: On authentication, we will require SAML SSO and RBAC for team members. Can Redwood integrate with Okta?
[04:02] Maya: Yes, SAML/Okta is supported. We'll send SSO guide. For RBAC you can configure roles in the console; enterprise customers can add SCIM provisioning.
[04:13] Priya: Do you provide audit logs for model inputs/outputs? We need to prove data lineage.
[04:19] Ravi: Audit logs are part of Private and can be enabled for Dedicated with extended retention add-on. We log request metadata, model version, timestamps; for full input/output retention it's configurable and we suggest encrypting logs with your KMS.
[04:34] Sam: Perf benchmarking — what's the plan?
[04:37] Maya: Ravi will provision a test environment with the model variants we recommend. We'll run 3 tests: single-request latency (cold+warm), sustained throughput at expected QPS, and quality regression against your eval set. We aim to produce a results spreadsheet within a week after we get sample traffic.
[04:54] Ravi: For benchmarks we'll use a small dedicated pool and a copy of your traffic replay; we'll instrument token-level timings and trace tail latencies. Expect a benchmark run to take 48-72 hours to collect stable stats.
[05:07] Lena: Any blockers we should know? Network peering to our VPC might take time.
[05:11] Maya: Good point — peering, firewall rules, and KMS trust relationship are typical blockers. We'll send a network checklist.
[05:19] Ethan: I'll add tasks in the onboarding doc and assign owners.
[05:22] Priya: Who signs the contract for Dedicated/Private? Legal is separate but I want to understand timelines.
[05:27] Maya: For Dedicated we can do an MSA + SOW; typical procurement takes 4-6 weeks for customers your size. If you want a Private deployment, lead time is longer depending on network and compliance checks. We'll share a contract draft.
[05:42] Sam: For the pilot success metric — if we hit p95 < 250ms and accuracy delta < 5% vs manual triage, we consider it successful.
[05:51] Maya: Noted. We'll codify that in the onboarding success criteria.
[05:55] Priya: Can we get a walk-through of the console and route-level dashboards?
[06:00] Ethan: Yes, we'll schedule a product demo next week focused on console, observability, and cost dashboards.
[06:08] Maya: Ok, let's recap next steps. Maya to send onboarding checklist, pricing matrix, SOC2 docs, and SSO guide by 2027-04-22. Ravi to provision test env after AtlasWell shares sample traffic; target benchmark run by 2027-05-03. Lena to share traffic sample and compliance contact by 2027-04-27.
[06:27] Priya: Sounds good. One more thing — do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models if load spikes?
[06:33] Ravi: Yes, rollout policies support canary weights, A/B, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or cached responses. We'll show you how to configure that in the console demo.
[06:45] Sam: Great. Anything else?
[06:47] Maya: That's it from us. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the demo.
[06:52] Priya: Thanks all.
[06:54] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — e.g., 'K V cache' appears in auto transcript instead of 'KV cache'; 'V P C' seen for VPC. Shared links referenced above.
